headline: Approved $340,000 Auer Family Boathouse acquisition, a 20-year battery storage deal with Kearsarge Energy, and the new AFSCME labor contract.
summary: The board approved several funding items on its consent and deliberative agendas, including a lease of 99 Intervale Road, a $7,200 sponsorship grant to Vermont Psychological Services, and $340,000 for the Auer Family Boathouse acquisition at 3181 North Avenue. It also approved a 20-year power purchase agreement with Kearsarge Energy for battery storage at the McNeil Generating Station, a $207,604.20 subrecipient agreement with the VT Network, a $1,100,000 flow monitoring contract with ADS Environmental Services, a $1,790,700 state loan and $103,400 VHB contract for the Manhattan Stormwater Outfalls project, and a new collective bargaining agreement with AFSCME.
decisions: Approved the lease of 99 Intervale Road to The Intervale Center and Gardens Alive and recommended City Council authorize CEDO to enter the lease.
Approved and recommended a $7,200 sponsorship grant to Vermont Psychological Services for psychological asylum evaluations.
Approved and recommended the City Council approve $340,000 from the Conservation Legacy Fund to acquire the Auer Family Boathouse parcel at 3181 North Avenue.
Approved and recommended a 20-year power purchase agreement with Kearsarge Energy for battery storage at the McNeil Generating Station.
Approved a Subrecipient Agreement with the VT Network for $207,604.20 for the Chittenden County Community Justice Center.
Approved a contract with ADS Environmental Services for flow monitoring services, not to exceed $1,100,000 over 5 years.
Approved a $1,790,700 Step III loan and a $103,400 amended contract with VHB for the Manhattan Stormwater Outfalls Rehabilitation Project.
Approved and recommended ratification of the collective bargaining agreement between the City of Burlington and AFSCME for July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2028.
